items.notes: Summary accurately describes the always-succeeding extractor (unapply always returns Some(x)). The claim that this makes Product3 usable in a pattern match (e.g. `case Product3(a, b, c) => ...`) is correct: Scala's product-match pattern binds via the _1.._N accessors that Product3 provides, so no Tuple-specific unapply is required. @tparam and @param entries are accurate, lowercase, and unpunctuated. Dropping @return is consistent with the house rule since the first sentence ('Returns the given product wrapped in a [[scala.Some]]...') already fully states the return value. Phrasing and structure match the analogous Product1/Product2 docs exactly, preserving in-file consistency.
